questions.question:
Choose the one word substitute for the below sentence.

Rohit generously supported those in need, always finding joy in Offering help through his thoughtful gifts and financial assistance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Philanthropist**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Philanthropist"** refers to a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, especially by donating money to charitable causes. (परमार्थी)
 
 
• **Example:** The billionaire was a well-known philanthropist who donated millions to education and healthcare initiatives.
 
 
• In the given sentence, Rohit is described as someone who supports those in need and enjoys offering help through thoughtful gifts and financial assistance. This aligns perfectly with the qualities of a philanthropist.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Philanthropist**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Benefactor** (सहायक): A person who gives money or other help to a person or cause.
 
 
• **Example:** The benefactor of the new hospital wing wished to remain anonymous.
 
 
 
 
• **Sponsor** (प्रायोजक): A person or organization that provides funds for a project or activity, often for promotional purposes.
 
 
• **Example:** The sports event was made possible by a generous sponsor.
 
 
 
 
• **Donor** (दाता): A person who donates something, especially money or blood.
 
 
• **Example:** The blood donor saved the life of an accident victim.

questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence.

options.text: Eating too much his health was spoiled.
Most people don't like being disturbed while they are working.
For a long time people thought that the world was fiat and that people could fall off the edge.
You have to be a millionaire to shop in Harrods. Everything is so expensive there.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To identify the incorrect sentence, let's analyze the grammatical structure and context of each option:**

__
 
• **Option 1: Eating too much his health was spoiled.**

 
 
• This sentence contains a **dangling participle**. The phrase "Eating too much" suggests that "his health" was doing the eating, which is logically impossible. A participle phrase at the beginning of a sentence must describe the subject that immediately follows.
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "Because he ate too much, his health was spoiled" or "Eating too much, **he** spoiled his health."
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Most people don't like being disturbed while they are working.**
 __
 
• This sentence uses the passive gerund "being disturbed" correctly to describe a general preference.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: For a long time people thought that the world was flat and that people could fall off the edge.**
 __
 
• This sentence correctly uses the past tense to describe a historical belief. (Note: "fiat" in the prompt is a common typo for "flat," but the grammatical structure remains sound).
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: You have to be a millionaire to shop in Harrods. Everything is so expensive there.**
 __
 
• This sentence uses a common hyperbole to describe the high prices at a well-known department store.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• __Therefore, out of the given options, only sentence 1 is grammatically incorrect__.

questions.question:
Identify the grammatical error in the sentence below.

The borrower must return the book will done with reading.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The grammatical error is located in the phrase "**the book will**."
 
• In this sentence, "**will**" is used incorrectly as a conjunction to join the two parts of the sentence.
 
• "Will" is a modal verb that typically indicates future tense and must be followed by a base verb, which is not the case here.
 
• To fix the error, "**will**" should be replaced with a temporal conjunction such as "**when**" or "**once**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The borrower must return the book **when** done with reading."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The borrower"** – This is the correct subject of the sentence and contains no errors.
 
• **Option 2: "done with reading"** – This phrase functions correctly as a reduced adverbial clause modifying the time of the action.
 
• **Option 3: "must return"** – This uses the modal verb "must" followed by the base verb "return" correctly to express obligation.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the word "arm" with a **different meaning** from the others?

options.text: He broke his arm while playing football.
The army's personnel developed advanced arms and missile systems.
During the conflict, both sides used highly advanced arms.
The nation's defense unit was trained to use scientifically advanced arms.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "He broke his arm while playing football."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"arm"** has multiple meanings in English. One of the meanings refers to the upper limb of the human body, which extends from the shoulder to the hand. (हाथ/भुजा)
 
 
 
• **Example:** He broke his arm while playing football.
 
 
 
• The other meaning of **"arm"** refers to weapons or military equipment used for defense or attack. (हथियार)
 
 
 
• **Example:** The army's personnel developed advanced arms and missile systems.
 
 
 
• In the correct answer, the word "arm" is used to denote the physical body part, while in the other options, "arms" refers to weapons. Thus, the meaning of "arm" in Option 1 is different from the meaning in the other options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "He broke his arm while playing football."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: "The army's personnel developed advanced arms and missile systems."**
 
 
• In this sentence, "arms" refers to weapons or military tools. (हथियार)
 
• **Example:** The arms used by the soldiers were state-of-the-art technology.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "During the conflict, both sides used highly advanced arms."**
 
 
• Here, "arms" also means weapons or tools used in combat. (हथियार)
 
• **Example:** Both nations invested heavily in advanced arms during the war.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "The nation's defense unit was trained to use scientifically advanced arms."**
 
 
• In this sentence, "arms" again refers to weapons or military equipment. (हथियार)
 
• **Example:** The soldiers were equipped with the latest arms and technology.

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct passive voice of the following sentence.

Why has Purusottam driven Parshuram out of Mainak's house?

options.text: Why has Purusottam been driven out of Mainak's house by Parshuram?
Why has Mainak been driven out of Purusottam's house by Parshuram?
Why has Purusottam been driven out by Parshuram of Mainak's house?
Why has Parshuram been driven out of Mainak's house by Purusottam?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "Why has... driven" is in the **Present Perfect** interrogative form.
 
• **Passive Voice Rule:** To convert a Present Perfect question into Passive Voice, the structure is: **Wh-word + has/have + Object + been + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject?**
 
• **Subject-Object Swap:** In the active voice, "Purusottam" is the subject and "Parshuram" is the object. In the passive voice, "Parshuram" must become the subject.
 
• **Verb Conversion:** The active form "has driven" becomes "has been driven" in the passive form.
 
• **Phrase Maintenance:** The prepositional phrase "out of Mainak's house" should remain attached to the action "driven" for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Why has Parshuram been driven out of Mainak's house by Purusottam?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrectly swaps the roles, suggesting Purusottam was the one driven out.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrectly introduces "Mainak" as the one being driven out, which changes the meaning of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** While grammatically closer, the placement of "by Parshuram" and "of Mainak's house" is awkward and incorrectly identifies Parshuram as the agent (the one doing the driving).

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form.**

The company's decision was made known to the public through a press release.

options.text: A press release made the company's decision known to the public.
The public was made known to the company's decision.
The company made its decision known to the public through a press release.
A press release was used to make the company's decision known.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "was made known" is in the **Simple Past Passive** voice.
 
• **Active Voice Rule:** To convert Simple Past Passive to Active, the structure changes from "was/were + V3" to the **Simple Past (V2)** form of the verb.
 
• **Identifying the Logical Subject:** Although the passive sentence focuses on "The company's decision," the logical "doer" of the action is "The company." Option 3 correctly identifies the company as the subject.
 
• **Verb Conversion:** The passive "was made known" becomes the active "made... known."
 
• **Completeness:** Option 3 includes all the original information, including the method ("through a press release") and the target audience ("to the public").

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The company made its decision known to the public through a press release."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** While grammatically active, it makes "A press release" the subject. While logically possible, Option 3 is a more direct transformation of the original sentence's intent.
 
• **Option 2:** This is still in the passive voice ("was made known") and incorrectly suggests the public was the thing being "made known."
 
• **Option 4:** This is also in the passive voice ("was used") and simplifies the sentence too much, losing the specific "to the public" context.

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

**__This aspects will be tested while dealing__** with the emerging scenario in our western neighbourhood.

options.text: This aspects will be testing while dealing
This aspects will be tester while dealing
This aspects would be tested while dealing
These aspects will be tested while dealing

questions.solution:

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**aspects**," which is plural.
 
• For plural subjects, the correct demonstrative pronoun to use is "**these**."
 
• The verb "**will be tested**" is correct as it indicates a future passive action.
 
• **Options 1, 2**, and **3** are incorrect due to grammatical errors in subject-verb agreement or incorrect tense usage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"These aspects will be tested while dealing with the emerging scenario in our western neighbourhood."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2: "This aspects will be tester while dealing"** is incorrect due to the use of "this" (singular) and "tester," which is grammatically incorrect as it is not a verb.
 
• **Option 3: "This aspects would be tested while dealing"** is incorrect because of the mismatch between "this" (singular) and "aspects" (plural). Additionally, "would" is not appropriate for a definite future scenario.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

He said that he had finished his work.

options.text: He said, "I have finished his work."
He said, "He has finished my work."
He said, "I have finished my work."
He said, "He had finished his work."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that he had finished his work.
 
• **Key Conversions from Indirect to Direct:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The third-person pronoun **"he"** (acting as the subject in the reported clause) refers to the speaker, so it changes back to the first-person **"I"** in direct speech.
 
• The possessive adjective **"his"** changes back to **"my"** to correspond with the subject "I."
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Past Perfect to Present Perfect):**
 
 
• When converting from indirect to direct speech, the past perfect **"had finished"** is typically reverted to the present perfect **"have finished"**.
 
 
 
• **Removal of Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is removed and replaced by a comma and quotation marks.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, 'I have finished my work.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it uses "his work," which would imply the speaker finished someone else's work.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses "He" and "my," suggesting a different person finished the speaker's work.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it maintains the past perfect tense and third-person pronouns, which is not how a person would naturally state their own action in direct speech.

questions.question:
Identify the correct use of a compound adjective from the passage.

Which of the following phrases from the passage is a compound adjective used to modify a noun?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3** i.e '**Post-independence era**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"post-independence"** is a **compound adjective** formed by joining two words with a hyphen to describe the noun **"era"**.
 
• Compound adjectives are used to give precise meaning and clarity by combining two or more words to modify a noun.
 
• Other options like **"urban women"** or **"traditional outfits"** contain single adjectives, not compound ones.
 
• Therefore, **"post-independence era"** is the correct example of a compound adjective modifying a noun.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban women:** "Urban" is a single adjective modifying "women", not a compound adjective.
 
• **Crop tops:** This is a noun phrase, not an adjective modifying another noun.
 
• **Traditional outfits:** "Traditional" is a single adjective modifying "outfits", not a compound adjective.

questions.question: Which sentence from the passage contains a relative clause?

options.text: Fashion is now seen as a means of self-expression.
Designers are reimagining the saree, giving it modern drapes.
Clothing often indicated a woman's marital status, community, and social standing.
Traditionally, Indian women wore sarees, ghagras, and salwar suits that varied greatly from region to region.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4** i.e '**Traditionally, Indian women wore sarees, ghagras, and salwar suits that varied greatly from region to region**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **relative clause** begins with a relative pronoun such as **"who, which, that"** and provides additional information about a noun.
 
• In this sentence, the clause **"that varied greatly from region to region"** modifies the noun **"sarees, ghagras, and salwar suits"**.
 
• This makes it a clear example of a relative clause functioning as an adjective clause.
 
• The other options do not contain relative pronouns or clauses; they are simple or participial constructions.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Fashion is now seen as a means of self-expression." → Simple sentence, no relative clause.
 
• **Option 2:** "Designers are reimagining the saree, giving it modern drapes." → Contains a participial phrase, not a relative clause.
 
• **Option 3:** "Clothing often indicated a woman's marital status, community, and social standing." → Descriptive, but no relative pronoun or clause.
 
• **Option 4:** Correct, because the clause **"that varied greatly from region to region"** is a relative clause modifying the noun phrase.

• **Example:** His skill in making wooden furniture shows true dedication to his craft.
 
 
 
• Hence, in the passage, "craftsmanship" clearly refers to **skill in making things**, highlighting the artistry of traditional Indian clothing.

questions.question: Which of the following describes "alma mater"?

options.text: A school or college that one one has attended

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. A school or college that one has attended**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"alma mater"** is a Latin phrase that translates to "nourishing mother" in English. It refers to the school, college, or university where one has studied and graduated. (हिंदी में: जिस विद्यालय या कॉलेज में किसी ने पढ़ाई की हो)
 
 
• **Example:** Harvard University is his alma mater, where he completed his graduation in 2005.
 
 
• It is a term often used with a sense of pride and affection for the institution where a person received their education. (हिंदी में: यह शब्द आमतौर पर शिक्षा प्राप्त करने वाले संस्थान के प्रति गर्व और स्नेह के भाव को व्यक्त करता है।)

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2 i.e. A school or college that one has attended**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** She spends most of her day at the place where she works, which is a software company.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A close friend** (हिंदी में: एक करीबी दोस्त): This refers to a person with whom one shares a strong bond of friendship, not an educational institution.
 
 
• **Example:** He considers John his close friend because they have known each other for years.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A foreign language** (हिंदी में: एक विदेशी भाषा): This refers to a language that is not native to a person or their country, not an educational institution.
 
 
• **Example:** She is fluent in Spanish, which is a foreign language in her country.
